acrid.definition: with a sharp biting taste, hot and peppery
acrid.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

adnate.definition: describes gills that are attached to the stipe along all or most of their height
adnate.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

adnexed.definition: narrowly attached; describes gills that are attached to the stipe along only a part of their height, or appear as though a small part of the gill had been cut away next to the stipe
adnexed.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

agaricoid.definition: Built like a typical gilled mushroom: a cap on a stipe, with gills underneath.

alder.definition: Decidious trees in the Alnus genus

anastomosing.definition: describes gills that split and re-join in network fashion, like a braided stream
anastomosing.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

angular.definition: describes pores that end in angles, as opposed to rounded pores

annulus.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

apical pore.definition: A single opening at the top of a puffball through which spores escape.

basal bulb.definition: A swollen, rounded base to the stipe.

bolete.definition: a fleshy mushroom with a tube layer on the underside of the cap
bolete.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

boletoid.definition: Built like a bolete: a cap on a stipe, with a spongy layer of tubes and pores underneath instead of gills.

bracket.definition: A shelf-like fruit body growing sideways out of wood, with no stipe.

broad.definition: Of gills, wide from edge to stipe. A width, not the spacing that crowded, close and distant describe.

bruises black.definition: Turning black where cut or handled.

bruises blue.definition: Turning blue where cut or handled.

bruises brown.definition: Turning brown where cut or handled.

bruises green.definition: Turning green where cut or handled.

bruises red.definition: Turning red where cut or handled.

bruises yellow.definition: Turning yellow where cut or handled.

buff.definition: a pale yellow color with slight grayish tones
buff.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

bulbous.definition: Swollen and rounded, usually at the stipe base.

buried wood.definition: Growing from wood buried in the soil, so appearing to grow from the ground.

burn site.definition: Growing on ground that has been burnt.

caespitose.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

campanulate.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

cantharelloid.definition: Built like a chanterelle: vase- or trumpet-shaped, with blunt forking ridges rather than true gills.

cap.definition: the broad expanded umbrella-like portion of a typical mushroom, which bears gills, tubes, spines, or a smooth surface on its underside
cap.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

cartilaginous.definition: rigid and brittle, breaking with a snap; usually in reference to a stipe
cartilaginous.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

clavarioid.definition: Club- or coral-shaped, with the spore-bearing surface on the outside of the branches.

clavate.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

close.definition: in reference to spacing of gills, farther apart than crowded, but closer together than subdistant
close.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

club.definition: An unbranched, upright, club-shaped fruit body.

clustered.definition: Growing in tight groups from a common base.

collybioid.definition: Built like a Collybia: a modest cap on a slim, central, cartilaginous stipe.

columella.definition: sterile stipe-like tissue within some false truffes or puffballs
columella.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

concentric.definition: Arranged in rings around a common centre.

conifer.definition: a cone-bearing tree, usually evergreen, such as pine, spruce, or Douglas-fir
conifer.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

convex.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

coral.definition: A branched, upright fruit body resembling marine coral.

corticioid.definition: Forming a thin crust flat against its substrate, with no cap and no stipe.

cortina.definition: A cobwebby partial veil of fine fibres, typical of Cortinarius.

crenulate.definition: scalloped, finely scalloped, usually in reference to the edge of a gill or cap
crenulate.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

crowded.definition: in reference to spacing of gills, packed closely together
crowded.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

crust.definition: A thin flat sheet of fungal tissue spread over its substrate.

cup.definition: A cup- or bowl-shaped fruit body, open at the top.

decurrent.definition: describes gills that are attached to, and extend down, the stipe
decurrent.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

depressed.definition: in reference to the cap, having the central portion sunken relative to the margin
depressed.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

distant.definition: in reference to spacing of gills, rather far apart
distant.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

dry.definition: Neither sticky nor moist to the touch.

duff.definition: plant litter making up the surface layer of forest soil; usually applied in conifer forests
duff.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

earthball.definition: A tough-skinned, roughly spherical fruit body with a dark spore mass inside.

earthstar.definition: A puffball whose outer layer splits into star-like rays that peel back from the spore sac.

emarginate.definition: Gills abruptly notched at the stipe.

entire.definition: even, smooth, not toothed or broken up; usually in reference to the cap or gill margin
entire.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

epigeous.definition: Fruiting above ground, in the ordinary way. The opposite of hypogeous.

equal.definition: of the same diameter throughout; usually in reference to a stipe
equal.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

eroded.definition: irregularly toothed; usually in reference to the gill edge
eroded.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

false gills.definition: Blunt, forking, vein-like ridges that look like gills but are folds of the cap surface.

false morel.definition: A brain-like or saddle-shaped fruit body superficially resembling a morel; several are dangerously toxic.

fan.definition: A flat, fan-shaped fruit body, usually attached at one edge.

farinaceous.definition: odor or taste like that of freshly ground meal; when strong, somewhat like that of cucumber or watermelon rind
farinaceous.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

fibrillose.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

fibrous.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

fleshy.definition: Soft and substantial, like a typical mushroom cap.

folds.definition: Shallow wrinkles or creases on the spore-bearing surface.

forking.definition: Splitting into two or more branches.

fragile.definition: Easily broken or crumbling; of a stipe or a ring that does not survive handling.

free.definition: describes gills that are not at all attached to the stipe along their height
free.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

fungus.definition: Growing on another fungus, as a parasite or a decomposer of it.

gasteroid.definition: Producing spores inside a closed fruit body, released when it opens, tears or is struck.

gelatinous.definition: Jelly-like in texture, often shrinking to a hard crust when dry and reviving when wet.

gills.definition: Thin blade-like plates under the cap, bearing the spores.

glabrous.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

glandular dots.definition: tufts of caulocystidia that exude a sticky fluid; usually in reference to the stipe of certain suilluses
glandular dots.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

gleba.definition: in gasteromycetes, the tissue in which the spores are formed; may include capillitium
gleba.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

granulose.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

greasy.definition: Faintly oily to the touch, without being properly viscid.

hardwood.definition: flowering trees with broad leaves such as alder, maple, madrone, and oak; may be deciduous or evergreen
hardwood.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

helvelloid.definition: Built like an elfin saddle or false morel: a lobed, saddle-shaped or brain-like head on a stipe.

hollow.definition: With a cavity running through it.

hydnoid.definition: Bearing spores on downward-hanging spines or teeth rather than gills or pores.

hygrophanous.definition: changing from translucent to opaque, and often markedly fading in color (expallent), upon drying; usually in reference to the cap surface
hygrophanous.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

hypogeous.definition: Fruiting underground, so it has to be dug for — the truffles and their relatives.

incurved.definition: With the margin bent inward but not tightly rolled.

infundibuliform.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

irregular.definition: Without a regular or predictable shape.

jelly.definition: A gelatinous fruit body, often shapeless, lobed or ear-like.

keratin.definition: Growing on hair, wool, feathers, horn or other keratin-rich remains.

lateral.definition: attached at one side, as in the short stipe of many shelf-fungi
lateral.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

latex.definition: watery or milky fluid; produced by lactariuses and certain other fungi
latex.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

living tree.definition: Growing on a tree that is still alive.

marginate.definition: having a distinctly marked border, such as a gill with differently colored edge or bulb on stipe bearing a sharply flaring rim
marginate.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

mild.definition: Without a sharp or distinctive taste.

morchelloid.definition: Built like a morel: a pitted, honeycombed head on a hollow stipe.

morel.definition: A hollow fruit body with a pitted, honeycombed head.

nidulariaceous.definition: Built like a bird's nest: a small cup holding egg-like peridioles that rain splashes out.

ochraceous.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

ovoid.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

partial veil.definition: Tissue covering the gills of a young mushroom, often leaving a ring on the stipe.

partially emergent.definition: Fruiting mostly below ground with the top breaking the surface.

peridiole.definition: small chambers in the gleba of some gasteromycetes, or the “eggs” of bird’s nest fungi; spores are produced within them
peridiole.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

pezizoid.definition: Cup- or disc-shaped, an ascomycete bearing spores on the open upper surface.

plane.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

pleurotoid.definition: Built like an oyster mushroom: a shelving cap with the stipe off to one side or absent.

plicate.definition: folded like a fan or pleated skirt
plicate.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

polypore.definition: A bracket fungus with a pored underside, usually on wood and usually without a stipe.

polyporoid.definition: Built like a bracket fungus: tough, usually growing from wood, with pores underneath.

pores.definition: The open ends of tubes on the underside, through which spores fall.

pruinose.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

puffball.definition: A rounded fruit body with spores formed inside, puffed out through a pore or tear.

rays.definition: The star-like arms formed when an earthstar's outer layer splits and peels back.

resupinate.definition: flat-lying fruitbody, with the upper “cap” surface attached to the substrate (usually a log) and fertile surface facing outward
resupinate.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

reticulation.definition: A raised net-like pattern, usually on the upper stipe.

rhizomorphs.definition: Cords of bundled mycelium at the base, like roots.

ridges.definition: Blunt raised folds bearing spores, as in the chanterelles.

ring.definition: membranous skirt-like remnant of a partial veil borne on a stipe
ring.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

rooting.definition: With a tapering base extending down into the substrate.

rubbery.definition: Springy and yielding, returning to shape — firmer than soft, not as stiff as tough.

saddle.definition: A lobed head folded like a saddle, typical of Helvella.

scabers.definition: Small dark tufted scales on the stipe, typical of Leccinum.

scaly.definition: Covered in flat or raised scales.

scrobiculate.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

sinuate.definition: Gills notched just before they meet the stipe.

slender.definition: Thin and narrow in stature, for the size of the cap.

smooth.definition: Without hairs, scales, ridges or roughness.

spore print.definition: The deposit of spores left when a cap is laid on paper, used to read their colour.

stinkhorn.definition: A fruit body that emerges from an egg and bears a foul-smelling spore slime that attracts flies.

stipe.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

striate.definition: having small parallel or radiating lines or grooves (“striped”); often in reference to a cap margin or spore
striate.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

stuffed.definition: Filled with soft loose tissue that may later hollow out.

subdecurrent.definition: Gills running only slightly down the stipe.

subdistant.definition: in reference to spacing of gills, farther apart than close, but closer together than distant
subdistant.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

teeth.definition: Downward-hanging spines that bear the spores.

toothed.definition: Bearing spores on downward-pointing spines or teeth.

tough.definition: Resistant to tearing; leathery rather than fleshy.

truffle.definition: A fruit body that matures underground and never opens.

trumpet.definition: A hollow, funnel- or trumpet-shaped fruit body open at the top.

tubes.definition: The layer of small vertical pipes under a bolete's cap, ending in pores.

umbonate.definition: With a raised boss or knob at the centre.

unchanging.definition: Keeping its colour when cut or handled.

universal veil.definition: Tissue enclosing the whole young fruit body, often leaving a volva and cap patches.

veil.definition: A layer of tissue covering part of the young fruit body, often leaving traces as it tears.

velvety.definition: Covered in a dense short pile, like velvet.

vinaceous.definition: said to be the color of red wine; in practice, not so deeply colored and with duller gray to brown tones, yielding more of a dark salmon-pink
vinaceous.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

viscid.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

volva.definition: remnants of a universal veil found at the base of the stipe
volva.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary

warts.definition: Raised lumps or patches on the surface, often veil remnants on a cap.

waxy.definition: Feeling greasy or wax-like, and often translucent.

zonate.definition: with concentric bands of different color or different shades of one basic color; usually in reference to the cap surface Stipe shapes. Illustration by Marsha Mello.
zonate.source: Mushrooms of the Pacific Northwest (2009), glossary
